# `gcp.backendservice`

A Backend Service defines a group of virtual machines that will serve traffic for load balancing. This resource is a global backend service, appropriate for external load balancing or self-managed internal load balancing. For managed internal load balancing, use a regional backend service instead. Currently self-managed internal load balancing is only available in beta. ~> **Note:** Recreating a `google_compute_backend_service` that references other dependent resources like `google_compute_url_map` will give a `resourceInUseByAnotherResource` error, when modifying the number of other dependent resources. Use `lifecycle.create_before_destroy` on the dependent resources to avoid this type of error as shown in the Dynamic Backends example.

| Tier | 1 (ruled: encoder (encoders/backend_service.go.tmpl) does two things, both caused by Terraform's schema, not the API. It nulls maxUtilization on any backend whose group is a network endpoint group, because Terraform's schema gives that field a default and the API rejects it for NEGs; this provider has no schema defaults, so the field goes out only if the user writes it, and then Google's own validation error names it. It also deletes the cdnPolicy TTLs under USE_ORIGIN_HEADERS, because Terraform sends a zero for an unset TTL; this provider never sends an unset field.
decoder (decoders/backend_service.go.tmpl) drops consistentHash from a read when localityLbPolicy is not MAGLEV or RING_HASH. Google keeps a stale consistentHash after the policy changes, and Terraform's next whole-object update would send it back and be refused. Our patch sends only the fields the diff changed, so a stale consistentHash is never sent unless the user changes it.
post_create and post_update (the same template, compute_backend_service_security_policy.go.tmpl) call setSecurityPolicy and setEdgeSecurityPolicy when security_policy or edge_security_policy changed. Discovery marks both fields "[Output Only]", so here they are output-only and the hook has nothing to act on.
THE BOUNDED GAP: a Cloud Armor policy cannot be attached from this type. It shows in state once attached some other way. Attaching one needs a setSecurityPolicy call, which is the same missing piece as setLabels.
) |
